name: Example: Computing the Image of a Point Under a Linear Transformation of a Plane
problem:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/11b0a0434116475ce544b737e282fd34f252aa781a72e7bdedf1d868d47087c0.png)

What are the coordinates of the point $B',$ the image of $B(2,-3)$ under the action of $\mathbf T?$
worked_solution:
To find the image of $B$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a column vector $\mathbf{x}$ containing the coordinates of $B{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/de0e0e242c55d338db39c80ce9b34c4a841aacef15a2368e1c00610ece9d2679.png)

Now, we compute the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $T\mathbf{x}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $T \mathbf{x},$ contains the coordinates of $B'.$ Therefore, $B'(3,-5).$
